questions.q: What are the five steps of the Power BI workflow, in order?
questions.explain: Get data, clean it with Power Query (Transform), relate and calculate (Model), build charts (Visualize), then share it (Publish) — the order this entire course follows.

questions.q: Which tool do you use for the Transform step?
questions.explain: Power Query Editor is where data gets cleaned and reshaped — the subject of Chapter 3.

questions.q: Why can't you skip straight from Get to Visualize without Transform and Model?
options: Fields may be the wrong data type, and visuals pulling from multiple tables need relationships defined first
Power BI Desktop technically prevents it with an error
You can skip them; they're purely optional cosmetic steps
Transform and Model are only needed for DirectQuery connections
questions.explain: Each step depends on the one before it: unclean data types cause chart problems, and visuals that combine fields from separate tables require a relationship between those tables first.

questions.q: Which chapter of this course covers the Model step in depth?
questions.explain: Chapter 4 covers fact/dimension tables, the star schema, and relationships — the Model step. DAX (Chapters 5-6) builds on top of it.

questions.q: What does the Publish step actually do?
options: Sends the report from Power BI Desktop to the Power BI service so others can access it
Saves the .pbix file to your local computer
Converts the report into an Excel file
questions.explain: Publish uploads your semantic model and report to a workspace in the Power BI service — the cloud platform where sharing, permissions, and scheduled refresh live (Chapter 9).
